chunks: (Moses) replied: "I did do that and I was in the wrong,

key_terms.الضَّالِّينَ: The astray / those who went wrong
key_terms.فَعَلْتُهَا: I did it (referring to the act of killing)

ai.seo_question: What did Prophet Moses say about his past action when commanded to return to Pharaoh?
ai.summary: In this verse, Prophet Moses (AS) reflects on his impulsive act of killing an Egyptian, recognizing it as a pre-prophetic error made while he was still among the 'misguided' or 'erring' before his divine commission. Shia scholars often highlight this as a moment of humble self-accountability, illustrating that even prophets undergo a process of spiritual refinement and are not immune to human frailty prior to receiving full guidance. This admission underscores the theme of divine mercy accepting sincere repentance and the transition from personal agency to prophetic authority.
